findings.title: Privileged mintFor() and burn() ignore the global `paused` flag and per-index `disabled` flag
findings.rootCauseClass: incomplete pause/disabled enforcement on privileged supply-changing entry points
findings.mergedDescription: Only the paid mint()/_executeMint() path is gated by require(!paused) and require(!config.disabled) (lines 171/174). The two privileged supply-changing entry points are not: mintFor(index,recipient) (206) checks only authorizedMinters[msg.sender] + that the index is registered, and burn(holder,tokenId,quantity) (341) checks only authorizedBurners[msg.sender]. Neither consults `paused` nor `config.disabled`. SECURITY-FOOTGUN LENS (code-scanner CODE-001): the only wired authorized minter in the design is NFTMigrator, so migrate()->mintFor() can keep minting V2 claim NFTs while the contract is paused and for an index the owner has explicitly disabled; the pauser/owner reasonably expect `paused` to stop ALL minting and `disabled` to block ALL new issuance, but the privileged paths bypass both. No untrusted party gains anything beyond what the trusted minter/burner already could, and migrator mints are 1:1 against burned V1 NFTs (no net claim inflation) -> Low, not higher. SPEC-CONFORMANCE LENS (story-faithfulness FAITH-003): the pause-bypass is DELIBERATE and faithful - the reverted story-033 explicitly justified a pause-exempt migration primitive ('migrations are a one-shot cleanup and must remain executable even if the standard mint path is paused'), and mintFor is that primitive - so pause-bypass is NOT a deviation. The DISABLED-bypass IS the Law-2 deviation: no story authorizes ignoring config.disabled, and it contradicts the documented semantics of the disabled flag ('new mints are blocked but existing NFTs remain valid'). An owner who disables a dispatcher index to block new mints would be surprised the privileged path still mints it.
findings.mergeNote: MERGE of CODE-001 (security footgun framing) + FAITH-003 (Law-2 spec-deviation framing) - confirmed same root cause: both target NFTMinterV2.mintFor/burn omitting the paused+disabled gates. Both framings preserved; the disabled-bypass is the unfaithful (Law-2) part, the pause-bypass is deliberate-by-design.

findings.recommendation: Add require(!configs[index].disabled) to mintFor so the kill switch is uniform across mint()/mintFor() (this closes the Law-2 deviation). Keep the deliberate pause-bypass but document it explicitly; consider whether burn should honor paused.

findings.title: setRatio accepts ratio == MAX_RATIO (50), contradicting the documented strict-less-than (<50) invariant
findings.rootCauseClass: off-by-one boundary operator (`>` vs `>=`) + stale/self-contradictory spec
findings.mergedDescription: setRatio uses `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert RatioTooHigh()` (MAX_RATIO=50), which ACCEPTS newRatio==50, and the constructor seeds DEFAULT_RATIO=50, directly contradicting three NatSpec docstrings (lines 23/42/76) and story-030 which state the ratio is strictly `< MAX_RATIO` (max 49). Commit 924b188 ('raised ratio because sUSDS appreciation') deliberately raised the default 30->50 and relaxed the check `>=`->`>`, but left every 'strictly < 50' docstring and the story-030 statement unchanged, so the spec is now internally self-contradictory: docs say <50, code permits ==50. Per the conflicting-sources rule the stale/ambiguous spec IS the finding. Security impact is none-demonstrated: ratio=50 means 50% of dispatched USDS accrues as phUSD mint-debt while (default donation disabled) 100% is pooled as sUSDS backing -> phUSD over-backed ~2:1, which is exactly the stated rationale for the raise. The hazard is a stale invariant misleading a future reviewer/integrator about the true cap.
findings.mergeNote: MERGE of FAITH-001 (faithfulness/spec view) + PM-05 (pattern INCORRECT-OPERATOR, off-by-one). Same single line (78), same root cause. SYMBOLIC-P2 (Halmos, PROVED) is verification context: it formally proves the reachable post-state is exactly [0,50] (50 reachable, 51 not) - confirms the off-by-one is real and BOUNDED, supporting Low. Do NOT emit FAITH-001 and PM-05 as two findings.

findings.ledgerMap: L-02 (qa-bundled, low) - 'setRatio accepts ratio == MAX_RATIO, contradicting documented strict-less-than invariant'. This is the faithfulness/pattern view of the SAME issue. Sanitizer should reconcile to L-02 and NOT emit a duplicate.
findings.lawNotes: Law 2 (spec deviation). Owner-set economic parameter; no permissionless path.
findings.recommendation: Either re-tighten to `newRatio >= MAX_RATIO` and lower DEFAULT_RATIO below 50, OR update the three docstrings + story-030 to state 50 is the valid maximum and fix MAX_RATIO's 'exclusive upper bound' wording.

findings.title: phUSD mint-debt accrues on GROSS dispatched USDS while a donation slice is permanently exported - under-backs phUSD when batchDonationSize + ratio > 100 (parameter-coupling footgun)
findings.severityNote: Downgraded from FAITH-002's potential-medium to Low on Tier-3 evidence: invariant-results pins the exact boundary (solvency holds iff d+r<=100; default d=0,r=50 is ~200% backed) and finds NO permissionless extraction path - the two knobs are owner-only, independent, in separate contracts. It is a non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope), not a Medium.
findings.rootCauseClass: value-flow accounting / un-coupled cross-contract parameters (gross-debt vs net-retained backing)
findings.mergedDescription: Per dispatch of `amount` USDS: donationUSDS = amount*batchDonationSize/100 is converted to USDC via Sky PSM buyGem and shipped to batchMinter (exported), so only poolingUSDS = (100-d)% is retained as sUSDS backing; independently the hook accrues phUSD mint-debt = amount*ratio/100 on the GROSS amount, and pull() later mints exactly that phUSD. batchDonationSize (BalancerPoolerV2, cap 100) and ratio (the Hook, cap 50) are set by SEPARATE owner setters in SEPARATE contracts with NO on-chain invariant linking them. Whenever batchDonationSize + ratio > 100, phUSD minted (ratio%) exceeds the USDS retained as in-protocol backing ((100-donationSize)%). story-034 is FAITHFULLY implemented (not an implementation gap); the hazard is the story's own design under an owner-chosen parameter combination. Tier-3 invariant test (forge+Medusa, 27910+ calls) confirms: d=40,r=50 -> 120% backed (PASS); d=50,r=50 -> exactly 100% (boundary); d=60,r=50 -> 80% backed / 20% uncovered with donation actually cleared (break); d=100,r=50 -> 0% backed (break). REFUTE-A (econ-scanner) establishes the retained-collateral/minted ratio is ARITHMETICALLY UNCHANGED from the pre-034 baseline already adjudicated as suppressed DEDUP-001 - story-034 changed the donation MECHANISM (AMM swap -> fixed-rate PSM) and TIMING, not the backing arithmetic - so this does NOT 'newly break' backing.
findings.mergeNote: MERGE of FAITH-002 (story-design-safety / Law-1 cross-ref) + CODE-001-sibling CODE-D01 (code-scanner deferral of the gross-vs-net asymmetry) + econ-scanner REFUTE-A residual-footgun note + pattern MR-01 (MINT-ON-DEMAND-OVERMINT). All four describe the same gross-debt-vs-exported-donation under-backing surface. Invariant-results.json is verification context that pins severity at Low.
findings.faithfulnessTag: F-02 (FAITH-002) - flows to spec-conformance report; lawImpacted=1 (story-design safety), conditional on owner parameter choice
findings.ledgerMap: DEDUP-001 (suppressed: 'phUSD unbacked mint - owner-driven, out-of-scope external backing model'). DO NOT silently collapse here. KEPT AS A DISTINCT CANDIDATE per Law-1 recall. SANITIZER MUST DECIDE: (a) collapse into the hard-suppressed DEDUP-001 (econ-scanner REFUTE-A verdict: still a duplicate of DEDUP-001, arithmetic unchanged from pre-034 baseline -> stays suppressed), OR (b) survive as a fresh Low operational-footgun given the NEW story-034 mechanism + the invariant-proven `batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100` guardrail (a concrete, in-protocol, owner-actionable safe-config rule that did not exist when DEDUP-001 was suppressed). Recommendation to sanitizer: lean (b) as a Low runbook/footgun finding carrying the proven guardrail, because the suppression rationale for DEDUP-001 (off-chain backing model) does not extinguish the NEW non-obvious cross-contract coupling hazard; but flag for human review.
findings.lawNotes: Law 1 cross-ref (story-design safety) but conditional on owner config; Law 3 footgun (two separately-tuned contracts, no linking invariant). NO permissionless trigger (invariant-confirmed).
findings.recommendation: Enforce batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100 on-chain (cross-check ratio when setting batchDonationSize), OR accrue mint-debt on net poolingUSDS rather than gross, OR document the backing invariant `phUSD_debt <= retained_sUSDS_backing` as the operator's solvency guardrail. Confirm whether batchMinter USDC remains protocol-owned (if so, no net leak).

findings.title: Single-sided sUSDS LP add (pool()) relies solely on a keeper-supplied minBPT with no on-chain price reference - batched adds are sandwichable (MEV treasury value-leak)
findings.severityNote: Footgun-escalable to Medium. Low because (a) real vault-enforced slippage protection (minBPT) is present, (b) pool() is permissioned (onlyAuthorizedPooler) so an attacker can only front-run a keeper's public tx, not initiate, (c) the structurally-identical class was adjudicated Low in L-03. Escalates only under a keeper footgun (loose/stale/zero minBPT) or a pathologically thin pool.
findings.rootCauseClass: missing on-chain slippage reference / off-chain-trusted bound (MEV LP-add sandwich)
findings.mergedDescription: pool(uint256 minBPT) drains the ENTIRE accumulated sUSDS balance and adds it as a single-sided AddLiquidityKind.UNBALANCED join into the 2-token sUSDS/phUSD Balancer V3 pool. The only value protection is minBptAmountOut = minBPT, a floor supplied entirely off-chain by the authorized pooler/keeper; there is no on-chain oracle/TWAP/spot lower bound. getIdealBPT() reads CURRENT pool state via router.queryAddLiquidityUnbalanced, so a keeper sizing minBPT off a fresh spot quote is sizing off a manipulable number. A single-sided join into a 2-asset pool is the most sandwich-prone LP shape (the join implicitly force-swaps ~half the sUSDS into phUSD along the curve). The H-02 fix (decouple pooling from per-mint dispatch) AMPLIFIES this: sUSDS now accumulates across many mints and is dumped in one large add, maximizing price impact. Extracted value per call is bounded above by (idealBPT_fair - minBPT); with a loose/zero minBPT the bound collapses. The harmed party is the protocol treasury (BPT custodied by the dispatcher, owner-withdrawn); individual minters hold no residual claim, so this is a treasury leak, not cross-user socialization.
findings.mergeNote: MERGE of ECON-001 (econ-scanner, Low) + PM-02 (pattern MISSING-SLIPPAGE, potential-medium guess). Same function, same root cause. The donation leg is NOT affected (story-034 routes it through fixed-rate Sky PSM, no curve).

findings.title: replaceDispatcher() carries the old per-index price to a new dispatcher whose primeToken() may differ - next mint() charges a stale, possibly mis-scaled price in a different token
findings.rootCauseClass: config carry-over across a dispatcher swap with a different prime token (cross-contract price-denomination mismatch)
findings.mergedDescription: replaceDispatcher swaps configs[index].dispatcher, dispatcherToIndex and tokenIdToDispatcher, but preserves configs[index].price/growthBasisPoints. In V2 the charged token is read at mint time from ITokenDispatcherV2(config.dispatcher).primeToken() (H-01 fix, line 177), so the SAME numeric `price` is now interpreted in the NEW dispatcher's prime-token units. If the replacement dispatcher's primeToken has different decimals or value (e.g. swapping an 18-dp USDS dispatcher for a 6-dp token dispatcher), the carried-over price is silently mis-scaled - over- or under-charging the next minters until the owner calls setPrice. The price field lives in NFTMinterV2 while its denomination is defined by whichever dispatcher is currently bound to the index. No external attacker; bounded by owner-trust, hence Low.
findings.mergeNote: Single-source live finding (CODE-002); no cross-agent merge but corroborated by Tier-1 LOCAL-NMV2-003. Distinguished from MR-05/C-01 below: C-01 tracks the GENERAL replaceDispatcher hazard (re-pointing token/metadata under existing holders). DD-05 is the DISTINCT price-denomination carry-over sub-issue (re-denomination of a persisted price), which C-01's description does not cover.
findings.ledgerMap: RELATES TO C-01 (qa-bundled centralization: 'Owner can replaceDispatcher at an existing index, re-pointing token/metadata under existing holders') but is a DISTINCT aspect (price re-denomination, not token/metadata re-pointing). Sanitizer to decide: add as a new sub-item under C-01, or emit as a fresh Low footgun. Flag for human review on the C-01 boundary.
findings.lawNotes: Non-obvious owner footgun (Law 3 in-scope): replaceDispatcher's name implies a like-for-like swap and gives no hint that price persists and is re-denominated.
findings.recommendation: Document the carry-over loudly, or have replaceDispatcher require an explicit new price argument (or reset price to 0 / re-emit PriceUpdated) so the operator must reconfirm price against the new primeToken.

findings.title: migrate() unbounded per-unit mint loop causes gas DoS for large V1 holders (+ index-0 late-registration brick)
findings.severityNote: Medium-class by impact, but LEDGER-TRACKED AS WONT-FIX. Carried here for provenance/recall only; DO NOT re-escalate - V1->V2 migration already executed and migrate() is no longer exercised on-chain. Code-scanner CODE-R05 refuted the double-mint angle (burn-before-mint makes each index idempotent); the only residual is the known gas-exhaustion, which has no new evidence of being live.
findings.mergedDescription: migrate() iterates i=1..v1.nextIndex() with external balanceOf/burn per index AND a nested inner loop minting one V2 NFT per unit of balance (v2.mintFor in a j<balance loop). The inner bound is the holder's per-index ERC1155 balance (unbounded) -> a large V1 holder can exceed the block gas limit and be permanently unable to migrate (M-01). Separately, a V1 dispatcher registered after setInitialized has indexMapping==0, making mintFor revert 'index not registered' (M-02 brick).
